name: KServe
supported_backends: none (orchestration layer - drives vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton)
supported_formats: passthrough (does not load weights - orchestrates inference engines)
notable_features: CNCF incubating project (joined 2025-11-11) - the Kubernetes-native serving standard
LLMInferenceService CRD with prefix-aware routing, disaggregated serving, and fine-grained GPU scheduling
InferencePool and InferenceModel CRDs for multi-model routing with EPP (Endpoint Picker Pod)
Direct KEDA scaling support (v0.21.0) with idleReplicaCount=0 for true scale-to-zero
Canary traffic splitting for inference services
NixlConnector for P/D engines so KV actually transfers
DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation) support via resourceClaims
OCI model delivery with measured startup benchmarks
6070 stars, active development with 100+ PRs per release
hardware_caveats: Kubernetes is not optional - the entire architecture is built around K8s CRDs and controllers
LLMInferenceService is v1alpha2 - still alpha API surface
Requires Envoy Gateway for traffic routing - additional infrastructure dependency
EPP (Endpoint Picker Pod) adds a hop to every request - latency cost for routing intelligence
KEDA integration is new (v0.21.0) and not yet battle-tested in production
Multi-node disaggregated serving requires RDMA-capable fabric
best_for: Kubernetes-native LLM serving with standardized APIs
Multi-model fleets where requests should route to the model with the best cache hit
Teams already invested in Kubernetes who want a vendor-neutral serving layer
Autoscaling on LLM-specific metrics (KV cache utilization, queue depth) via KEDA
avoid_for: Non-Kubernetes environments - the entire architecture assumes K8s
Single-model single-node serving where the overhead is not justified
Teams needing a stable GA API - LLMInferenceService is still alpha
Low-latency single-request serving where the EPP hop matters
notes: KServe is the Kubernetes-native inference orchestration layer. It does not run inference itself - it drives vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, and Triton Inference Server. The LLMInferenceService CRD is the key abstraction for LLM-specific features: prefix-aware routing (send requests to the replica with the best KV cache hit), disaggregated serving (separate prefill/decode pools), and fine-grained GPU scheduling. The EPP (Endpoint Picker Pod) is the routing brain - it makes per-request routing decisions based on cache state, load, and latency. KServe v0.21.0 (2026-09-25) added direct KEDA scaling with idleReplicaCount=0 for true scale-to-zero, which is the first production-ready path for LLM-specific autoscaling on Kubernetes.
